The Scoring Fit on the Subspace That a Kink Leaves Free

Source: R/iwls.R
iwls_tied.Rd

Runs iwls_fit() on \(\beta = \beta_0 + N w\), with \(N\) a basis of the directions that the kink constraints and the held coordinates leave free (null_basis()), and returns the point reached in the coefficients.

Usage

iwls_tied(
  obj,
  beta,
  method,
  n,
  pieces_at,
  Ak,
  frozen,
  backup_at = NULL,
  newton_at = NULL,
  switch_at = NULL,
  switch_after = Inf,
  kinks_at = NULL,
  damp_on_reject = TRUE
)

Arguments

obj

The objective, with fn and gr.

beta

The point \(\beta_0\).

method

The Iwls() method.

n

The number of observations.

pieces_at, backup_at, newton_at, switch_at, kinks_at

As iwls_fit() takes them, in the full coefficients.

Ak

The rows of the kink constraints at beta.

frozen

The positions held.

switch_after, damp_on_reject

As iwls_fit() takes them.

Value

NULL where the constraints leave no direction free, and otherwise a list with par, the coefficients reached, value, converged and score, the reduced fit's.

Details

The reparametrization is linear, so the reduced problem's pieces are the full problem's pieces carried through \(N\): the square-root design and the penalty's factor are multiplied by \(N\) on the right, the assembled matrix becomes \(N^\top A N\), the gradient \(N^\top g\) and the full Hessian \(N^\top H N\). A kink met in the reduced problem adds its row, carried through \(N\), in the same way.

See also

iwls_fit(), kink_constraints()
